title: A collaborative workflow between pathologists and deep learning for the evaluation of tumour cellularity in lung adenocarcinoma.
authors: Sakamoto, Taro; Furukawa, Tomoi; Pham, Hoa H N; Kuroda, Kishio; Tabata, Kazuhiro; Kashima, Yukio; Okoshi, Ethan N; Morimoto, Shimpei; Bychkov, Andrey; Fukuoka, Junya
one_liner_zh: 该文利用深度学习评估肺癌肿瘤细胞含量，属于病理图像分析，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: AIMS: The reporting of tumour cellularity in cancer samples has become a mandatory task for pathologists. However, the estimation of tumour cellularity is often inaccurate. Therefore, we propose a collaborative workflow between pathologists and artificial intelligence (AI) models to evaluate tumour cellularity in lung cancer samples and propose a protocol to apply it to routine practice. METHODS AND RESULTS: We developed a quantitative model of lung adenocarcinoma that was validated and tested on 50 cases, and a collaborative workflow where pathologists could access the AI results and adjust their original tumour cellularity scores (adjusted-score) that we tested on 151 cases. The adjusted-score was validated by comparing them with a ground truth established by manual annotation of haematoxylin and eosin slides with reference to immunostains with thyroid transcription factor-1 and napsin A. For training, validation, testing the AI and testing the collaborative workflow, we used 40, 10, 50 and 151 whole slide images of lung adenocarcinoma, respectively. The sensitivity and specificity of tumour segmentation were 97 and 87%, respectively, and the accuracy of nuclei recognition was 99%. One pathologist's visually estimated scores were compared to the adjusted-score, and the pathologist's scores were altered in 87% of cases. Comparison with the ground truth revealed that the adjusted-score was more precise than the pathologists' scores (P < 0.05). CONCLUSION: We proposed a collaborative workflow between AI and pathologists as a model to improve daily practice and enhance the prediction of tumour cellularity for genetic tests.
abstract_zh: 目的：报告癌症样本中的肿瘤细胞含量已成为病理学家的强制性任务。然而，肿瘤细胞含量的估计往往不准确。因此，我们提出了一种病理学家与人工智能（AI）模型之间的协作工作流程，用于评估肺癌样本中的肿瘤细胞含量，并提出一种将其应用于常规实践的方案。方法与结果：我们开发了一个肺腺癌定量模型，在50例病例上进行了验证和测试，并建立了一个协作工作流程，病理学家可以访问AI结果并调整其原始肿瘤细胞含量评分（调整后评分），该流程在151例病例上进行了测试。调整后评分通过与手动标注苏木精-伊红切片并参考甲状腺转录因子-1和napsin A免疫染色的金标准进行比较来验证。用于训练、验证、测试AI和测试协作工作流程的肺腺癌全切片图像分别为40、10、50和151张。肿瘤分割的敏感性和特异性分别为97%和87%，细胞核识别的准确性为99%。一名病理学家的视觉估计评分与调整后评分进行了比较，病理学家的评分在87%的病例中发生了改变。与金标准的比较显示，调整后评分比病理学家的评分更精确（P < 0.05）。结论：我们提出了一种AI与病理学家之间的协作工作流程，作为改善日常实践和增强基因检测肿瘤细胞含量预测的模型。
